title: On-call and Incident Response Playbook
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview

Purpose
- This playbook defines Redwood Inference's standard incident lifecycle, runbook templates, on-call rotation rules, postmortem process, game day guidance, and customer-facing status and communication templates. It is intended to be the single source of truth for operational incident response.

Scope
- Applies to all production services and customer-facing endpoints across Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Goals
- Restore service to acceptable levels quickly and safely.
- Communicate clearly to internal stakeholders and customers.
- Capture root cause and deliver corrective actions to prevent recurrence.

Incident classification and severity
- SEV0 (P0): Complete outage or data loss affecting most or all customers, critical business impact. Requires immediate paging and executive notification.
- SEV1 (P1): Severe degradation or partial outage impacting a significant subset of customers or critical workflows. High priority pager.
- SEV2 (P2): Functional degradation without major customer impact. Ticketed response within hours.
- SEV3 (P3): Minor issues, operational tasks, or non-urgent bugs.

SLOs and targets
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA): 
  - SEV0/SEV1: 5 minutes.
  - SEV2: 1 hour.
- Mean time to restore (MTTR) targets:
  - SEV0: 60 minutes.
  - SEV1: 4 hours.
  - SEV2: 24 hours.

Roles and responsibilities
- Primary on-call (Primary): First responder for alerts and incident triage. Responsible for initial remediation and escalation.
- Secondary on-call (Secondary): Backup to Primary; takes over if Primary is unavailable or during escalation.
- Incident Commander (IC): Owns incident coordination, timeline updates, and cross-team decisions for SEV1+/SEV0. Usually appointed within first 10 minutes for SEV0/SEV1.
- Communications Lead: Drafts internal and external updates and publishes to the status page.
- Subject Matter Experts (SMEs): Service owners and engineers who provide technical fixes.
- Postmortem lead: Owns the RCA write-up and follow-up actions.

Alerting and escalation policy
1. All production monitoring alerts publish to PagerDuty (or equivalent) with a runbook link and runbook priority.
2. If no acknowledgement within MTTA, alert escalates to Secondary, then to Engineering Manager, then to On-call Director.
3. Use alert suppression sparingly; a suppression requires an owner and an expiration time.

Runbook structure and conventions
- Every runbook for a service must include:
  - Title and service owner
  - Symptoms and alert IDs
  - Impact assessment checklist
  - Step-by-step mitigation steps (numbered)
  - Key dashboards and queries
  - Safe rollback steps and post-recovery validations
  - Links to related docs and postmortem history

Sample runbook entry: inference-api-service
- Service owner: API Platform team
- Symptoms: 5xx rate above 3% sustained for 5 minutes, latency p95 > 1.5s
- Dashboard: ApiRequestsOverview > production > last 60m
- Immediate steps:
  1. Acknowledge pager.
  2. Check recent deploys: curl -s https://deployments.internal/api/latest | jq .
  3. Verify pod health: kubectl get pods -n inference -l app=inference-api
  4. If OOMs or CrashLoopBackOff, capture logs: kubectl logs -n inference -l app=inference-api --tail=200
  5. If CPU saturated, scale replicas: kubectl scale deploy/inference-api --replicas=6 -n inference
  6. If config change suspected, revert to previous config tag and monitor.
- Post-recovery validation:
  - p95 latency back within 10% of baseline for 15 minutes
  - No increase in 5xx errors for 30 minutes

Incident lifecycle and playbook (step-by-step)
1. Detection and Triage (0-5 min):
  - Primary acknowledges. Triage severity, impact, affected customers, and assign role for Communication.
2. Contain and Mitigate (5-30 min):
  - Execute relevant runbook steps. If service-level mitigation insufficient, escalate to IC.
3. Stabilize (30-120 min):
  - Implement temporary workaround or rollback; reduce blast radius.
4. Recover (1-6 hours):
  - Restore full functionality and perform validation checks.
5. Communicate and Close (after recovery):
  - Publish status page update, internal summary, and create postmortem if SEV1+/SEV0.

Communication templates
- Status page template (short form):
  - Summary: We are investigating increased errors for inference-api affecting text generation requests.
  - Impact: A subset of customers may observe 5xx errors and elevated latency.
  - Current status: Mitigation in progress, rollback initiated.
  - Next update: in 30 minutes or when status changes.

- Customer-facing incident email (use only for SEV1+/SEV0):
  - Subject: Incident update: [service] degraded - [short impact summary]
  - Body:
    - What happened: Brief factual summary.
    - Impact: Which customers/features were affected.
    - Mitigation: Actions taken so far.
    - ETA: Estimated recovery time if available.
    - Contact: Support link and severity escalation contact.

- Internal update (first 15 min):
  - Channel: #incidents (internal slack) and pagerduty notes.
  - Format: short bullets - time, severity, impact, owner, immediate mitigation.

Post-incident: postmortem process
- Postmortem required for SEV1 and SEV0 incidents. SEV2 considered case-by-case.
- Timeline:
  - Draft due: within 48 hours of incident resolution.
  - Internal review: within 7 days.
  - Public summary (customer-facing): within 10 business days if customers were impacted.
- Postmortem template must include:
  - Summary and timeline of events
  - Impact and scope (customers, duration, data loss if any)
  - Root cause analysis (technical RCA and contributing factors)
  - Corrective actions and owners with due dates
  - Preventative measures and follow-ups

Example postmortem action items:
- Improve alerting thresholds for model-loading failures - owner: model-serving - due: 2026-03-31
- Add automated canary deploy for inference-api - owner: eng-platform - due: 2026-04-15

On-call rotations and rules
- Rotation cadence: 1 week per rotation for Primary on-call. Week starts Monday 00:00 UTC and ends Sunday 23:59 UTC.
- Secondary rotation follows the same cadence with offset.
- Shift length: 7 days for primary; handover window of 30 minutes at shift change.
- Swap policy: swaps are allowed with both people updating the on-call calendar and notifying Engineering Manager and Secondary.
- PTO and blackout windows: planned major releases or holiday periods may have blackout policies; team leads must publish exceptions to the on-call schedule at least 72 hours in advance.
- Compensation and support: on-call stipend and incident pay are defined in 03_benefits-and-perks.

Handover checklist
- Outstanding alerts or incidents and their status
- Recent deploys and known risks
- Any scheduled maintenance or blackout windows
- Contactable secondary and SMEs
- Calendar updated and Slack statuses set

Game days and exercises
- Frequency: Quarterly team game days for core production services; annual full-scale company-wide exercise simulating multi-service outage.
- Scenario examples: model-serving cache corruption, cross-region network partition, and degraded GPU fleet capacity.
- Goals: Validate runbooks, test cross-team coordination, measure MTTA/MTTR, and surface tooling gaps.
- Post-exercise: write an after-action report with owners and remediation dates.

Tools and dashboards
- PagerDuty: primary alerting and escalation.
- Statuspage (or equivalent): public and internal incident pages.
- Grafana: service dashboards and playbook-linked panels.
- Kibana/Elasticsearch: logs for triage.
- Internal runbook repository: eng-platform/runbooks (link in related pages).

Retention and compliance
- Incident logs, chat transcripts, and postmortems retained for 2 years for internal audit.
- Customer-facing summaries retained per legal and compliance guidance.

Ownership and continuous improvement
- eng-sre owns the playbook.
- Quarterly review: this document and associated runbooks will be reviewed quarterly or after any SEV0/SEV1 incident.
- Metrics to track: MTTA, MTTR, number of SEV1/SEV0 incidents, percent of incidents with postmortems completed on time.

Appendix: Quick reference CLI commands
- Check pod health: kubectl get pods -n <namespace> -l app=<service>
- Stream logs: kubectl logs -n <namespace> deploy/<deployment> -f --tail=200
- Check recent deploys: curl -s https://deployments.internal/api/latest | jq .

Appendix: Postmortem checklist
- Include timeline with timestamps and actor annotations
- Link to all command outputs and logs used in triage
- List action items with owners and due dates
- Mark actions as verified when completed and link to changesets or tickets

Contact matrix
- Pager on-call: listed in PagerDuty schedules
- Engineering Manager escalation: em-oncall@redwood-inference.internal
- Incident exec notification: exec-notify@redwood-inference.internal
